title: What's answer engine optimization, and why does it matter now?
dek: Search is turning into conversation. Being the source an AI assistant quotes is the new first page.
summary: Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of writing and marking up pages so AI assistants can find, trust and quote them. It rewards a direct answer near the top, clear question headings, and structured data that names the author and publisher.

hero.alt: The Growth Momo, cut from blue and kraft paper, tending a seedling

body.heading: What changed about search?
paragraphs: People increasingly ask a question and read one composed answer instead of scanning ten links. The assistant still reads the web; it simply chooses a handful of sources to lean on.
That makes the job less about ranking for a phrase and more about being the clearest, most attributable answer to a question.

body.heading: What does an answer engine look for?
paragraphs: A short, plain answer early on the page. Headings phrased the way people ask. Named authors with a real role, a named publisher, and dates that say how fresh the answer is.
Structured data (JSON-LD) turns those facts into something a machine can verify rather than guess.

body.heading: Where should a team start?
paragraphs: Pick the ten questions your clients ask most. Answer each in two sentences at the top of a page, then go deeper below. Mark it up, and measure which answers get cited.

faq.question: Is AEO different from SEO?
faq.answer: It builds on SEO. The foundations are the same; AEO adds a stronger emphasis on direct answers, question headings and machine readable attribution.

faq.question: What's GEO?
faq.answer: Generative engine optimization: the same idea applied to AI systems that write answers, with extra weight on being quotable and clearly sourced.
